text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you recall any trauma or insect bites at that site?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use for uveitis, you are immunocompromised. Has this lesion ever been biopsy or cultured, and do you have any fever or systemic symptoms like joint pain or eye redness?

REQUEST TEST: Blood work (CBC, ESR, CRP, Glucose)
REQUEST TEST: Tissue biopsy of the lesion with special stains (Fungal/Giemsa) and culture.
